Q: Perfect forwarding - what's it all about? A:

Quoting Session Announcement: Adventures in Perfect Forwarding:

Perfecting forwarding is an important C++0x technique built atop rvalue references. It allows move semantics to be automatically applied, even when the source and the destination of a move are separated by intervening function calls. Common examples include constructors and setter functions that forward arguments they receive to the data members of the class they are initializing or setting, as well as standard library functions like make_shared, which “perfect-forwards” its arguments to the class constructor of whatever object the to-be-created shared_ptr is to point to.

Q: Reading in XML data in python A:

The data needs to be fixed at source. You could replace the LEFT/RIGHT DOUBLE QUOTATION MARKs with regular QUOTATION MARKs easily on the client side BUT that would not help with, for example:

<item name="Birth” Date type="xs:string" length="162"/>

or

<item name=“Stat”us type="xs:string" length="162"/>

Having said that, if these are the only 2 anomalies, then you could do some text replacement based on these known patterns

Q: simple/fast way to transfer files from Linux to Windows A:

I think rsync should by one of the best choice for your job.

And yes, rsync work sequentially, but there are some way of improvement!

Have a look at 3 - 4 tricks for speeding up rsync.! There are four different things to consider:

    1. Copying from/to local network: don't use ssh!
    1. Using zstandard zstd for high speed compression
    1. Multiplexing rsync to reduce inactivity due to browse time
    1. Important step to speed up rsync process: avoid to slow him down!!

Q: Unable to locate Attribute with the given name [XXX] on this ManagedType [XXX] at PageRequest.of() properties A:

The resolution algorithm checks the domain class for a property with that name, but uncapitalized, so it searches for messageSequenceID instead of MessageSequenceID.

Follow the naming convention in Java and use variables that start with lowercase letters to avoid problems.

Use messageSequenceID instead of MessageSequenceID in your domain model.

Q: I get error process /bin/sh -c did not complete successfully when building docker on arm A:

The problem is with the platform you are specifying for the image you are trying to pull. You are facing this issue because the arm64v8/debian:11-slim image doest not have an image for linux/arm64 architecture. The arm64v8 images are for the Apple silicon hosts i.e. currently M1 and M2 based macs

You can solve this problem by using the following pull statement in the Dockerfile:

FROM --platform=linux/arm64 debian:11-slim AS deps

RUN ls /

This would fix the issue as the debian dockerhub repository has all the arch needed for debian:11-slim.
